data.title: Peer-to-Peer Transfer Chain (Smurfing Pattern)
data.description: Detects chains of peer-to-peer transfers across multiple accounts where funds move through a sequence of intermediary accounts (A to B to C to D). This smurfing pattern is used to layer fraud proceeds through multiple hops, making tracing difficult.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Peer-to-Peer Transfer Chain (Smurfing Pattern)")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: selection_p2p | count() by account_id > 3 and selection_chain | count(distinct counterparty_account_id) by account_id > 2")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
(event_type="P2P_TRANSFER" OR event_type="INTERNAL_TRANSFER" OR event_type="ZELLE_SEND" OR event_type="VENMO_TRANSFER")
transaction_amount>=500
inbound_event="P2P_CREDIT"
outbound_event="P2P_DEBIT"
| stats dc(counterparty_account_id) as unique_counterparty_account_id by account_id
| where unique_counterparty_account_id > 2

falsepositives: Group event organizers collecting and redistributing shared expenses
Family members transferring funds between accounts for household management
